 SUBJECT:  SECOND READING OF ORDINANCE NO.___ ADDING SECTION 4-38

 Recommendation:

 Introduce for a second reading, read by title only, and waive further reading of the
 attached Ordinance No. ___, entitled “AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE
 CITY OF LYNWOOD, COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES, STATE OF CALIFORNIA, ADDING
 SECTION 4-38 “SERVICE PROVIDER WORKER RETENTION” TO CHAPTER 4
 “LICENSING AND BUSINESS REGULATIONS” OF THE LYNWOOD MUNICIPAL CODE”.

 Background:

 The City awards numerous contracts every year to various service providers and contractors
 to perform essential and critical services and governmental functions. The effective and
 efficient performance of these services is highly dependent upon skilled and experienced
 workers capable of executing the necessary work in a timely and competent manner. Any
 changes in the personnel of these service providers can have an effect on the quality of
 services provided by the City, whether due to a change of ownership of the existing service
 provider or the subsequent award of a contract to a different service provider.

 The City finds that the solicitation and procurement of new service providers is beneficial to
 the City’s overall economic health and provides the opportunity for other businesses to benefit
 from City service contracts. The City also recognizes that these benefits are not necessarily

City Council City Council Regular Meeting
  7
  diminished by the retention of workers experienced in performing these duties as it allows for
 the City to utilize those workers’ expertise and knowledge in the effective performance of such
 duties. Whenever there is turnover related to the performance of these functions, there is an
 adjustment period for new workers to be able to perform these functions with the same
 expertise and effectiveness as their predecessors. There is also a loss of institutional
 knowledge accrued through the experience and longevity of the prior employee. Replacement
 of these highly experienced and highly skilled workers may affect the success and
 performance of various City projects, services, and functions.

 The retention of the experienced workers also reduces the possibility of labor disputes and
 disruption of valuable City services. The minimization of such disruptions provides the City and
 the public with confidence that these services will continue seamlessly through any transition
 of ownership or change in providers. It will also reduce any impacts associated with
 unemployment due to such transitions or changes. The City recognizes that such efforts to
 reduce unemployment are a benefit to the City and the community in general.

 Discussion and Analysis:

 The proposed Service Provider Worker Retention Ordinance would require that certain
 existing service providers provide the City and any successor service provider with the contact
 information of any displaced worker due to a change in the ownership of the existing service
 provider, or a change in the company providing such services. It would require that the
 successor service provider offer any displaced workers employment a 90 day “transition”
 period, at which point the successor service provider can evaluate the displaced worker for
 consideration of continued employment.

 This would not apply to professional or special services providers as defined in Lynwood
 Municipal Code (“LMC”) §6-3.1, with the exception of “consultant” and “security services”. The
 successor service provider may not discharge any displaced worker during the transition
 period except for cause, as defined by wrongful termination case law. In the event that less
 displaced workers are required to perform the scope of work of the successor service, any
 reduction in the number of displaced workers must be approved by the City Manager, and any
 displaced workers must be retained by seniority. No reduction in displaced workers wages or
 benefits are allowed under the Ordinance, nor will any waiver of these rights by displaced
 workers be valid.

 The penalties for any violations, including discrimination or retaliation against displaced
 workers filing a complaint pursuant to this Ordinance, include all legal and equitable remedies
 at law, including back pay, reinstatement, injunctive relief, attorneys’ fees and punitive
 damages. A civil right of enforcement is available to displaced workers, but no criminal
 penalties. Any violations of this Ordinance would also allow the City to terminate the contract
 and withhold payments to the successor service provider and consider the violations in the

City Council City Council Regular Meeting
  8
  evaluation of the providers performance.

 The Ordinance also allows for the City to waive or modify any or all of the provisions of this
 Ordinance upon approval of the City’s Finance Committee and the City Council by majority
 vote. In the event of a deadlocked vote by the Finance Committee, the City Council may
 approve any waiver or modification by majority vote.

 The City Council introduced the ordinance for a first reading at the June 4, 2024. The City
 Council modified the draft ordinance to include limiting the obligation to provide the same
 wages and benefits to the displaced workers by the new SSp to 90 days. The ordinance was
 voted on with the modified language.

 Fiscal Impact:

 There may be some increase costs associated with proposals from successor contractors,
 however the City may benefit financially from the retention of skilled and experienced workers
 providing the same services during such transition periods.

  RECITALS

  WHEREAS, the City of Lynwood (“City”) enters into numerous contracts each year
with companies to provide services necessary to ensure the efficient and effective
delivery of essential services by the City; and

  WHEREAS, the City Council of the City of Lynwood (“City Council”) desires to
adopt an ordinance requiring certain business that benefit from City service contracts to
comply with worker retention policies including policies addressing any changes in
ownership or changes in service contractors; and

  WHEREAS, the City Council finds that in order to promote continuity and ensure
the effective transition of those entities providing City services, it is beneficial to the City
and general public to promote the hiring of experienced workers to perform such services
during periods of transition of ownership of services providers or a change to the
contractors hired to perform such services; and

  WHEREAS, the City Council finds that this Ordinance is beneficial for the
preservation of the public welfare, health and safety of residents living within the City of
Lynwood.

  All legal prerequisites to the adoption of this Ordinance have occurred.

  NOW, THEREFORE, THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNWOOD DOES
HEREBY ORDAIN AS FOLLOWS:

  Section 1. The City Council hereby finds and determines that all of the above
Recitals are true and correct and incorporates such Recitals into this Ordinance.

  Section 2. The City Council hereby amends Chapter 4 “LICENSING AND
BUSINESS REGULATIONS” of the Lynwood Municipal Code to add Section 4-38
“SERVICE PROVIDER WORKER RETENTION” to read as follows:

  4-38
  SERVICE PROVIDER WORKER RETENTION

4-38.1 Statement of Policy.

effective and efficient performance of these services is highly dependent upon skilled and

to the City’s overall economic health and provides the opportunity for other businesses to
benefit from City service contracts. The City also recognizes that these benefits are not
necessarily diminished by the retention of workers experienced in performing these duties
as it allows for the City to utilize those workers’ expertise and knowledge in the effective
performance of such duties. Whenever there is turnover related to the performance of
these functions, there is an adjustment period for new workers to be able to perform these
functions with the same expertise and effectiveness as their predecessors. There is also

affect the success and performance of various City projects, services, and functions.

any transition of ownership or change in providers. It will also reduce any impacts
associated with unemployment due to such transitions or changes. The City recognizes
that such efforts to reduce unemployment are a benefit to the City and the community in
general.

4-38.1 Definitions.

Change in provider shall mean any change in the existing service provider of City’s
contracted services to a successor service provider.

Change in ownership shall mean the assignment, alienation, transfer, sale, acquisition,
or disposition of a controlling stake or substantially all of assets of the existing service
provider by another entity, including but not limited such transfer through consolidation,
merger, reorganization, or bankruptcy.

City shall mean the City of Lynwood.

Contracted services shall mean services provided by a Service Provider under contract
with City for a cost above $300,000 for a period of twelve (12) consecutive months.
Contracted services shall not include professional or special services as defined under
chapter 6-3.1 of this code, however the terms “consultant” and “security services” shall

  2
  11
 not be considered professional or special services for the purpose of this section. The
City Manager, with the consent of the Finance Committee, shall have the discretion to
determine whether a certain service is considered a contracted service under this
ordinance pursuant to section 4-38.7. In the absence of a determination by the City
Manager regarding whether a certain service is considered a contracted service, the City
Council shall have the authority to make the determination by a majority vote of the City
Council.

Existing Services Provider or ESP shall mean the service provider contracted to provide
contracted services to the City prior to any change in ownership or change in provider
event.

Entity shall mean a person or individual, sole proprietor, partnership, limited partnership,
limited liability company, company, corporation, agency, association, trust, estate, joint
venture, or any other commercial or legal entity, whether domestic or foreign, but shall
not include other governmental agencies or public institutions.

Displaced worker shall mean any person or individual performing contracted services for
the City on behalf of an existing service provider, or any its subcontractors hired to
perform work under such contract. This does not apply to exempt employees under the
Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) or any person or individual who was not employed by
the ESP for a minimum of thirty (30) days prior to the execution of the Succession event.

Service provider shall mean any entity under contract with the City to provide contracted
services.

Successor service provider or SSP shall mean the entity that provides the same or
substantially the same contracted services to the City as the existing service provider
pursuant to any change in ownership or change in provider event.

Succession event shall mean the effective date of the document effecting a change in
ownership; or in the event of a change of services, the date of upon which the City
provides notice to the existing service provider that City has entered into a contract with
a successor service provider.

Transition period shall mean the period as described under section 4-38.3 of this chapter.

4-38.3 Displaced Worker Retention.

a.  Within ten (10) days of a succession event, the ESP must provide the SSP and the
City Manager a list of all of its displaced workers providing contracted services which were
subject to the change in provider or the change in ownership. The list shall include:

    Each displaced worker's name; and
    Last known address, email and phone number if available; and
    Date hired by the ESP; and

  3
  12
     Each displaced worker’s job classification at the time of the transfer.

b.  If the identity of the SSP is not known at the time of the succession event, such
information shall be requested from the City Manager. The SSP shall offer employment
to all displaced workers via certified mail, and if available via email or telephone, within
ten (10) days of being awarded the contracted services or a succession event, whichever
is sooner. The letter shall require the displaced worker to return a signed copy of the
letter to ESP indicating whether he or she has accepted or declined the offer. If the
displaced worker fails to submit a signed and accepted offer letter within ten (10) days of
displaced worker’s receipt of the offer letter, the offer shall be deemed as declined by the
displaced worker. The SSP shall provide copies of all offer letters and certified mail
receipts to the City Manager.

c.  To the extent feasible, SSP’s contracted services must be performed by displaced
workers, however, SSP shall not be required to unnecessarily create additional positions
to perform the contracted services. In the event SSP desires to reduce the amount of
work hours or positions utilized to perform SSP’s contracted services, the SSP must
obtain written approval from the City Manager and hire workers based on seniority
pursuant to section 4-38.4.

d.  The SSP may not discharge any displaced worker without cause for at least ninety
(90) days from the date on which the SSP actually begins providing contracted services
(the “transition period”). “Cause” as used in this Section shall mean in good faith and
based on a fair and honest reason, and not for reasons that are trivial, arbitrary or
capricious, unrelated to business needs or goals, or pretextual.

e.  At the expiration of the transition period, the SSP shall conduct a written
performance evaluation for each displaced worker retained by SSP. If the displaced
worker’s performance evaluation is satisfactory or better, SSP shall offer the displaced
worker continued employment with SSP subject to Section 4-38.5.

4-38.4 Preferential Hires.
a.  If, after the expiration of the transition period, the SSP determines that fewer
positions are needed to deliver and maintain the contracted service, the SSP shall retain
displaced workers by seniority.

b.  Seniority shall be determined by reference to the collective bargaining agreement
covering the displaced workers, if one exists, or, if no such agreement exists, then by
reference to the initial hire date with the ESP of each displaced worker. Any displaced
workers not retained by the SSP shall be placed on a preferential hiring list and
considered by the SSP for any job openings that may arise.

4-38.5 Wages and Benefits of Displaced Workers.

SSP must provide all displaced workers covered by this section 4-38 with wages and
benefits at a value of not less than the greater of those (a) in effect at the time of the

  4
  13
 termination or expiration of ESP’s contract or effective date of the change of ownership
or (b) in any collective bargaining agreement applicable to the displaced workers
employment with the ESP. Wages and benefits include all wages or compensation
referenced in the existing collective bargaining agreement including provisions
addressing how overtime shall be calculated, employer and employee contributions for
medical insurance and retirement benefits, any tool, shoe or uniform allowance, sick
leave, vacation time and personal or family leave. However, nothing in this ordinance will
be construed to require the maintenance of wages and benefits beyond the 90-day
transition period by the new SSP.

4-38.6 Retaliation and Discrimination.

a.  No ESP or SSP may discriminate against any person for filing a complaint,
participating in any investigation or proceeding relating to the enforcement of these
provisions, or pursuing any remedies available at law or equity for any violation of this
section 4.38 including any harassment, abuse, threats, discharge of duties, or reduction
in work hours or duties.

b.  Any waiver by a displaced worker of any or all of the provisions of this section 4.38
shall be deemed contrary to public policy and shall be void and unenforceable, except
where such waiver occurs in a bona fide collective bargaining agreement. Any attempt by
an ESP or SSP to have a displaced worker waive his or her rights given by this section
4.38 shall constitute a willful violation of this provisions included herein.

4-38.7 Enforcement.

a.  The City reserves the right to waive or modify any or all the provisions of this
section 4-38 with respect to any service provider upon a finding that it would not be in the
best interest of the City. Any waiver or modification shall require approval by the City
Council by a majority vote of the City Council.

b.  Any displaced worker claiming a violation hereunder, may bring an action against
the existing service provider or successor service provider in the Superior Court of the
State of California to enforce the provisions of this Section 4-38. The penalty for any
violation of this section 4-38 shall be for an amount equal to 90 days of the displaced
worker's average regular rate of pay, and any other actual damages or legal or equitable
remedies, including but not limited to reinstatement, injunctive relief, and back pay. This
section further authorizes the awarding of punitive damages for willful violations of this
section 4-38. Any plaintiff that successfully enforces his or her rights pursuant to this
section 4-38 shall be entitled to reasonable attorney's fees, expert witness fees, and costs
of litigation. Violations of this section 4-38 are declared to irreparably harm the public and
covered employees generally. Notwithstanding any provision of this code or any other
law to the contrary, no criminal penalties shall attach for any violation of this section 4-38.

 The Community Development Department has learned more about the services provided by

 Development has researched additional opportunities available for streamlining the collection
 of Cannabis annual and quarterly fees.

 Over the past couple of years, the City has adopted multiple cannabis ordinances resulting in
 the potential approval of 20 cannabis non-retail businesses and 5 retail cannabis businesses.
 The multi-year City process has resulted in a potential maximum of 25 cannabis business in
 the City. Community Development is responsible for the administration of the permits,

 license process (initial application and renewals). Lynwood Businesses have transitioned
 seamlessly to obtaining the Business Licenses online and the online portal has provided the
 end-user the ability to make payments from anywhere, saving time and money to the
 businesses and City. Community Development is proposing to incorporate the online Hdl

 The City of Lynwood envisioned a booming Cannabis industry that once awarded a

 Keeping track of the operators, owners and chasing down businesses is more than our
 Community Development and Finance Division staff can manage in addition to other daily
 duties. New tools are necessary to better manage the Cannabis industry fee collection.

 In March, 2024, Community Development requested a Proposal (RFP) from Hdl for an
 additional online service to assist in the cannabis administration and fee collection solution.
 Hdl has a Tax & Fee Administration service division that specializes in the collection of
 Cannabis fees. This solution integrates seamlessly with our Business license system and
 financial systems. Hdl's experienced revenue team can handle all aspects of operations
 compliance and collection of fees via software hosting, reminders, and collections. This allows
 staff to focus its efforts on other areas of importance, inspections, permitting, and compliance
 inspections.

 Staff followed the purchasing ordinance section 6-3.9 Professional/Special Services when
 reviewing the qualifications, cost, and RFP process. Hdl currently has a contract with the city
 to administer the business license permits and therefore they are in possession of all the
 vendors information as the Cannabis businesses are required to obtain business license
 permits. Hdl's administration will increase revenues, decrease staff costs, and improve
 customer service.

 Staff is recommending approval of the second amendment to add the additional
 module/service. This online module will be customized and added to our business license

 Cuellar. The persons elected to fill these seats will serve a four year term, expiring November
